subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: The High Line: Rails to Park
description: A short lesson to help you apply The High Line: Rails to Park.

hook.text: An abandoned elevated railway in Manhattan was scheduled for demolition. Wildflowers had already moved in.

buildup.text: Two residents formed a nonprofit to save it. They raised $150 million to turn the tracks into a park.

discovery.text: The High Line opened in 2009 — a one-mile elevated garden with native plants growing through the old rails.

twist.text: It triggered $2 billion in new development. Surrounding rents doubled. The neighborhood gentrified rapidly.

climax.text: Cities worldwide copied the idea. But most lack the High Line's proximity to wealthy neighborhoods.

punchline.text: A park for everyone. That raised rents for everyone too.

quiz.question: What unintended consequence did the High Line cause?
options: Increased crime rates in surrounding neighborhoods
Rapid gentrification and doubled rents in the area
Traffic congestion from tourists blocking nearby streets
